scripts.name: Indo-Pak (DigitalKhatt)
scripts.description: DigitalKhatt's Indo-Pak typesetting: subscript alef (U+0656), no alef wasla, Arabic Extended-B marks
scripts.note: Al-Fatiha follows the Indo-Pak segmentation: the basmala is unnumbered, so verse 1 is 'al-hamdu lillahi rabbi al-'alamin' and the last two verses are held separately, where the Hafs scripts make the basmala verse 1 and hold the final two together. Every chapter has the canonical count; only chapter 1's verse labels differ. No basmala is embedded in any verse. The text uses Arabic Extended-B marks (U+089C, 2,098 of them), which not every font covers: Noto Naskh Arabic and DigitalKhatt's own fonts cover every codepoint here, while Amiri renders U+089C as a missing glyph. Coverage is not shaping: a font that has the glyph still positions these marks by its own rules.

bismillah.source: The line the source prints under every surah header, outside the ayahs; the same form as the Hafs Nastaliq text.

license.attribution: Qur'anpedia.net (https://quranpedia.net); the dump version is recorded per snapshot in /meta/sources.json

scripts.note: Indo-Pak (KFGQPC Nastaleeq) is Quranpedia mushaf 3, the Hafs text in Nastaleeq with Hafs verse numbering. scripts.name: al-Duri
scripts.description: Quranpedia mushaf 6: al-Duri ʿan Abi ʿAmr with its own 6,218-ayah source count and per-ayah mapping to Hafs numbering

license.attribution: Qur'anpedia.net (https://quranpedia.net); the dump version is recorded per snapshot in /meta/sources.json

scripts.note: al-Duri ʿan Abi ʿAmr is a different riwayah, not an orthography: the pinned Quranpedia mushaf 6 contains 6,218 source ayahs. Forty-four chapters differ from the Hafs count; each verse's `number_in_hafs` preserves the source mapping. Al-Mulk has 31 ayahs here: the source splits Hafs 67:9 after نَذِيرٞ, which al-Susi, the other riwayah of Abu ʿAmr, does not.

mapping_coverage_exceptions.reason: source bismillah is unnumbered; retain source map without inventing Hafs 1

bismillah.source: Quranpedia's own `bismillah` field for this mushaf, printed outside the ayahs.

scripts.name: QPC Hafs (KFGQPC)
scripts.description: Quranpedia mushaf 2: the King Fahd Complex's Uthmanic Hafs ʿan ʿAsim text, the one Quran.com and KFGQPC's own apps use, with Hafs numbering

license.attribution: Qur'anpedia.net (https://quranpedia.net); the dump version is recorded per snapshot in /meta/sources.json

scripts.note: KFGQPC's Uthmanic Hafs text (Quranpedia mushaf 2), Hafs numbering, 6,236 ayahs. The basmala is verse 1 of Al-Fatiha only; no other verse 1 carries it, as in the Indo-Pak (KFGQPC Nastaleeq) script and unlike the Tanzil scripts, which prefix it to the first ayah of every surah except At-Tawbah. Uses KFGQPC's own mark encoding, so its bytes differ from Tanzil's while the letters agree.

scripts.note: Shuʿbah ʿan ʿAsim (Quranpedia mushaf 9): a different riwayah, not an orthography. It shares the Kufi count with Hafs, so verse ids are Hafs ayah numbers and `number_in_hafs` is always the verse's own id. The basmala is verse 1 of Al-Fatiha only.
